reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) demonstrates ML's general utility for predicting alloy mechanical properties and discusses surrogate models for strength/ductility trade-offs, but none provides specific prior support for the key premises about multi-fidelity FE-ML integration, its accuracy gains, or its application to fracture toughness in hierarchical heterostructures. The premises are largely unsupported by the referenced passages.
premises: Low-fidelity FE simulations can rapidly approximate global stress fields and mechanical response in heterogeneous microstructures.
Localized high-fidelity FE analyses at crack-sensitive regions can capture microscale fracture phenomena missed by low-fidelity models.
Machine learning regression can map FE-derived descriptors and microstructural features to macroscopic properties (E, σy, toughness).
The multi-fidelity surrogate approach will reduce computational cost by ~two orders of magnitude versus full-scale CALPHAD/first-principles simulations.
The integrated framework will achieve ±5–7% prediction error for Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness in HfNbTiVAl10.
